newsitem.title: PERU: Six foreign firms interested in Peru's Mahr Tunel.
newsitem.headline: Six foreign firms interested in Peru's Mahr Tunel.

text.p: State miner Centromin said Friday the upcoming privatization of its Mahr Tunel SA company, which controls two mines, had attracted the interest of six foreign and three domestic companies.

Centromin named the interested bidders as Switzerland's Glencore International, Australia's Savage Resources Ltd, Mexico's Industrial Penoles SA and Grupo Mexico S.A., the United States' Sunshine Mining and Refining Co, and Sweden's Boliden.
Local companies Minsur SA, Volcan and Morococha SA are also interested in bidding.
Centromin will formally take offers on June 16 and announce the winner June 20.
Mahr Tunel SA controls the San Cristobal and Andaychagua mines, which lie close to each other in the central Peruvian highlands.
Last year, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver, while Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore with silver, lead and zinc.
